title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
subtitle: a moist date cake soaked with warm brown-sugar toffee sauce: the coziest Christmas dessert
imageAlt: A square of dark date cake drenched in glossy toffee sauce in a white dish on a navy napkin
servingsNote: 9 squares from a 20 cm pan, with sauce for all

beforeYouStart.text: Set the butter and eggs out 30 minutes ahead.
Oven at 180°C (350°F), with a buttered 20 cm (8-inch) square pan ready.

steps.title: Soak the dates
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a 20 cm (8-inch) square pan. Pour the boiling water over the dates, stir in the baking soda and stand 10 minutes, then mash roughly with a fork.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Beat the butter and brown sugar 2 minutes, until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, and stir into the butter mixture. Stir in the dates and their liquid; the batter will be loose.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Scrape into the pan and bake 30–35 minutes, until a toothpick in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Toffee sauce
steps.text: Meanwhile, bring the butter, brown sugar, cream and salt to a boil in a saucepan, stirring, and simmer 3 minutes until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Soak and serve
steps.text: Poke the warm cake all over with a skewer and pour about a third of the sauce over. Let it soak 10 minutes, then cut into 9 squares and serve with the rest of the warm sauce.

fixIt.fix: It came out too early. Bake until a toothpick comes out clean from the very centre.
It boiled too hard. Whisk in 1–2 tbsp cream over low heat until smooth.
Stir until the sugar fully dissolves before it boils.
Overbaked. Pour on more sauce and let it soak; check it at 30 minutes next time.

saleTip: Dates are cheapest in the bulk aisle and on sale before Christmas. Brown sugar and butter are the rest, both December sale staples.
swap: No cream: use ½ cup evaporated milk in the sauce. It's a little less rich but just as glossy.
leftovers: Rewarm squares with a spoon of sauce in the microwave 30–40 seconds.
doneness: A toothpick in the centre comes out clean and the top springs back when pressed.
source: Based on tested sticky toffee pudding methods (BBC Good Food, Canadian Living): dates softened with boiling water and baking soda, a creamed batter baked at 180°C (350°F), and a butter, brown sugar and cream sauce.
prepAhead: Bake the cake and make the sauce up to 3 days ahead; keep both covered in the fridge. Rewarm the cake covered at 160°C (325°F) 15 minutes and the sauce on low.
reheat: Covered, at 160°C (325°F) 15 minutes, or single squares in the microwave 30–40 seconds. Warm the sauce on low.

basic.note: The same cake with a simpler milk toffee sauce.

stepNotes.4: Basic: use milk and simmer 4–5 minutes; it's a thinner sauce.

fancy.note: Toasted pecans and a scoop of vanilla ice cream melting into the sauce.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: while it bakes, toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium 3–4 minutes, until fragrant, then chop.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Top each warm square with a small scoop of ice cream, a spoon of sauce and the toasted pecans.

plating: Ice cream off-centre so the sauce pools beside it.

why.0-2: Baking soda softens the dates' skins so they melt into the cake and darken it.
why.0-0: Dates make the cake moist and toffee-flavoured without tasting like fruit.
why.1-2: Cream gives a thick, glossy sauce that soaks in without making the cake soggy.

funFact: Sticky toffee pudding is a modern classic: it was popularized in the 1970s at the Sharrow Bay hotel in England's Lake District.

keeps.note: keep the sauce in its own container, in the fridge or freezer
keeps.thaw: Overnight in the fridge, then rewarm
